premise: A staged hostage-video parody. A tradesman delivers implausibly glowing praise of his employer while two coworkers stand just out of shot holding tools on him. The humour is that he appears to be speaking under duress.
mechanism: Bound-hands pun: a coil of cable clenched in both fists at chest height reads as tied wrists, on screen the entire runtime
Content/affect mismatch: flat, resigned delivery of implausibly positive claims
Edge intrusion: tools enter the frame margins from the first second, so unease precedes understanding
Late reveal: a single cut at 85% widens to confirm what the edges implied

elements.what: seated tradesman, work polo, talking straight to lens
elements.function: the coerced speaker; carries the affect

elements.what: coil of white flat electrical cable gripped in both fists, wrists close together
elements.function: BOUND-HANDS PUN. Without the captors this prop is meaningless — it is not decoration, it is the joke

elements.what: forearm and hands gripping a steel claw hammer, cropped by the left frame edge
elements.function: visible coercion; the reason the praise is being given
elements.evidence: left edge at t=2.0s, confirmed by crop

elements.what: arm and cordless rotary hammer with long bit, cropped by the right frame edge, pointed inward
elements.function: second coercion source; motivates the subject's sideways eye-flick
elements.evidence: right edge at t=2.0s, confirmed by crop

elements.what: stud framing, brick, blown-out window, debris
elements.function: establishes trade context and justifies the tools

elements.what: subject glances off-frame toward a tool, then back to lens
elements.function: acknowledges the threat without naming it

performance.note: affect is load-bearing: a pleasant delivery destroys the premise even if every element is present

composition.shot_size: medium, roughly mid-thigh to just above the head
composition.subject_share: subject occupies most of the frame height
forbidden: full body with large ceiling visible
composition.note: a wide shot breaks the gag twice: it shrinks the hands below legibility and it reveals there is nothing at the edges

must_be_true: A naive viewer can tell the man is being made to speak against his will
At least one tool is visible intruding at a frame edge in the first second
The subject's hands read as bound or restrained
The subject does not appear happy
forbidden_assertions: nobody at the edges of frame
_note_forbidden: Do NOT list a bare 'no other people' here. Suppressing crowd creep REQUIRES the prompt to say no additional people, and a blunt phrase cannot distinguish that from deleting the two captors. Captor presence is enforced by G2 element coverage instead.
known_blind_spots: audio: cannot be evaluated by the vision pipeline; dialogue realism unverified
comedic timing: no metric; beat placement judged only by human viewing
